################################################################################################
#
#  Dayside magnetopause crossings (MPCs) identified in Time History of Events and
#  Macroscale Interactions during Substorms (THEMIS) five spacecraft data
#  between 2007 and mid-2022.
#
#  THEMIS measurements retrieved from http://themis.ssl.berkeley.edu/data/themis
#  via the PySpedas package https://github.com/spedas/pyspedas.
#
#  The description of the identification process using a Random Forest Classifier
#  can be found in section 3 of:
#    Grimmich, N., Plaschke, F., Archer, M. O., Heyner, D., Mieth, J. Z. D., Nakamura, R., & Sibeck, D. G. (2023).
#    Study of extreme magnetopause distortions under varying solar wind conditions.
#    Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics, 128, e2023JA031603. https://doi.org/10.1029/2023JA031603.
#
#  The columns contain:
#    column 1: MPC number
#    column 2: identified crossing time in UT
#    column 3: observing spacecraft
#    column 4: prediction probability of the crossing
#    column 5: stand-off distance of MP during the observation
#    column 6: deviation of the stand-off distance from the Shue et al. (1998) model
#    column 7: latitude postion of the observing spacecraft in degree
#    column 8: longitude postion of the observing spacecraft in degree
#    column 9: radial position of the observing spacecraft in Earth radii
#
################################################################################################
